info.title: HTTP Arena API
info.description:
Endpoint contract for HTTP Arena benchmark implementations.

Each path is used by one or more test profiles. Frameworks must implement the endpoints for every profile they subscribe to in `meta.json`, following the **Standard** or **Tuned** rules documented per operation (plus the **Engine** or **Infrastructure** rules where an entry is of that kind). The validation script (`validate.sh`) runs these endpoints against a live server before any benchmark results are accepted. Most parameters it sends are drawn at random on every run, so a response prepared in advance cannot pass.

All numeric fields are integers - no floats. JSON responses use lowercase field names. Endpoints that query Postgres return HTTP 200 with an empty list rather than an error when no rows match or the database is unavailable.

**Port mapping:**
- `8080` - HTTP/1.1 plaintext (baseline, limited-conn, pipelined, async, json-comp, async-db, fortunes, the latency profiles and the WebSocket profiles) and cleartext HTTP/2 for gRPC (unary-grpc)
- `8081` - HTTP/1.1 + TLS, ALPN `http/1.1` (json-tls, static-tls, 8gbit)
- `8082` - HTTP/2 cleartext with prior knowledge (baseline-h2c, json-h2c)
- `8443` - HTTP/2 + TLS over TCP (baseline-h2, static-h2, unary-grpc-tls) and HTTP/3 over QUIC on UDP (baseline-h3, static-h3)
- `9000` - opt-in TLS hardening listener (`"tls_check": true` in `meta.json`), HTTP/1.1 + TLS with its own certificate directory `/certs-tls`. Validation only, nothing is measured.

TLS certificates are mounted at `/certs/server.crt` and `/certs/server.key`. The dataset is mounted at `/data/dataset.json` and the static files at `/data/static/`.

**gRPC** and **WebSocket** endpoints cannot be fully modeled in OpenAPI 3.0; their contracts are described in the operation descriptions and linked documentation.

Gateway and production-stack endpoints are documented in the separate [gateway spec](/openapi-gateway.json).

servers.description: HTTP/1.1 plaintext (and h2c for gRPC) - default port for all benchmark containers
HTTP/1.1 + TLS - json-tls, static-tls and 8gbit profiles (ALPN: http/1.1)
HTTP/2 cleartext (h2c) - baseline-h2c and json-h2c profiles (prior-knowledge, no ALPN)
HTTP/2 + TLS (TCP) and HTTP/3 / QUIC (UDP) - baseline-h2, static-h2, unary-grpc-tls, baseline-h3 and static-h3 profiles
HTTP/1.1 + TLS - opt-in TLS hardening checks (tls_check), validation only

tags.name: Baseline
tags.description: Primary throughput benchmark over persistent keep-alive connections (4,096 connections). The same `/baseline11` endpoint also drives the **limited-conn** profile (connections closed and re-opened after 10 requests) and the fixed-rate **latency-1m**, **latency-10k** and **latency-500k-8cpu** profiles, which send `GET /baseline11?a=1&b=2` at a pinned rate and rank on the CPU spent to serve it.

tags.name: Pipelined
tags.description: HTTP pipelining benchmark. 16 requests are sent back-to-back on each connection before awaiting responses, isolating raw I/O throughput from application logic. Reference-only for frameworks - not part of their composite score; scored for infrastructure entries.

tags.name: Async Delay
tags.description: A flat 10 ms wait named in the route, over 32,000 held connections. Measures what a framework does with a request it cannot answer yet - its concurrency model rather than its parser.

tags.name: JSON
tags.description: JSON serialization workload. Loads a 50-item dataset at startup and computes a per-request `total` field. Used by **json-comp** (port 8080, client sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip, br`, server must compress) and **json-tls** (port 8081, HTTP/1.1 + TLS, no compression). The **json-h2c** profile serves the same endpoint over HTTP/2 cleartext (see H2 JSON).

tags.name: 8Gbit Echo
tags.description: A 10 KB body is posted over HTTP/1.1 + TLS on port 8081 and must come back verbatim, loading ingest and egress at once. The rate is pinned at 50,000 req/s over 512 connections, so the profile is scored on cost (CPU and latency) rather than throughput.

tags.name: Static Files over TLS
tags.description: Serves 20 static assets (CSS, JS, HTML, fonts, SVG, WebP, JSON) from `/data/static/` over HTTP/1.1 + TLS on port 8081, in a round-robin pattern with `Accept-Encoding: br;q=1, gzip;q=0.8`. Pre-compressed `.gz` and `.br` sidecars are available on disk for the 15 text files. Reference-only for framework and engine entries; scored for infrastructure.

tags.name: Async Database
tags.description: Async Postgres range query benchmark. Exercises async I/O scheduling, connection pooling, and JSON serialization with live database queries against the 100,000-row `items` table. Reference-only - not part of the composite score.

tags.name: Fortunes
tags.description: Template rendering benchmark: query 200 rows from Postgres, append one row at request time, sort, and render an HTML table with auto-escaping. Reference-only - not part of the composite score.

tags.name: H2 Baseline
tags.description: HTTP/2 baseline - same `a + b` sum as `/baseline11` but served over HTTP/2 with 100 concurrent streams per connection. Two sub-profiles: **baseline-h2** (port 8443, TLS + ALPN `h2`) and **baseline-h2c** (port 8082, h2c prior-knowledge, no TLS).

tags.name: H2 Static Files
tags.description: Same `/static/*` endpoint as Static Files over TLS, served over HTTP/2 + TLS on port 8443 with 32 concurrent streams per connection.

tags.name: H2 JSON
tags.description: Same `/json/{count}` endpoint as the JSON profiles, served over HTTP/2 cleartext (h2c) on port 8082 with 32 concurrent streams per connection.

tags.name: H3 Baseline
tags.description: Same `/baseline2` endpoint as the H2 baseline, served over HTTP/3 / QUIC on UDP port 8443 with 64 concurrent streams per connection. Only frameworks with native QUIC support participate.

tags.name: H3 Static Files
tags.description: Same `/static/*` endpoint, served over HTTP/3 / QUIC on UDP port 8443 with 64 concurrent streams per connection.

tags.name: gRPC Unary
tags.description: Unary gRPC RPC (`GetSum`) with 100 concurrent streams per connection. Two profiles with the same RPC and load: **unary-grpc** over HTTP/2 cleartext (h2c, prior-knowledge) on port 8080, and **unary-grpc-tls** over HTTP/2 + TLS (ALPN `h2`) on port 8443.

tags.name: WebSocket Echo
tags.description: WebSocket echo benchmark. Each connection upgrades via HTTP/1.1, then exchanges `"hello"` text frames. Three profiles share the `/ws` endpoint: **echo-ws** (one message in flight), **echo-ws-pipeline** (16 messages in flight) and **echo-ws-limited** (connection closed and re-upgraded after 10 messages). Note: the message exchange after the `101` response cannot be modeled in OpenAPI 3.0 - only the HTTP upgrade handshake is documented here.

get.description:
Returns `a + b` as plain text with `Content-Type: text/plain` (a `charset` suffix is allowed).

Used by the **baseline** profile (4,096 keep-alive connections, mixed with the two POST forms below), the **limited-conn** profile (same requests, connections closed after 10 requests) and the fixed-rate **latency-1m**, **latency-10k** and **latency-500k-8cpu** profiles, which send `GET /baseline11?a=1&b=2` at a pinned rate. The latency profiles add no code, but they charge every CPU cycle the server spends - busy-wait loops, spin-polling and fixed-cadence timers are all counted there.

Validation also sends randomized operands, lower-cased header names, and requests split into fragments at every byte offset, so the parser must reassemble requests across reads.

**Standard:** Must use the framework standard HTTP server with default configuration. No custom TCP tuning, no experimental flags, no worker count beyond framework defaults.

**Tuned:** May adjust worker counts, thread pools, TCP socket options, and use framework-specific performance flags. Custom buffer sizes allowed.

**Infrastructure:** Configuration is free. The endpoint must be answered by a module or handler loaded into the server itself, not proxied to an application process behind it.

post.summary: Sum query parameters and plain-text body value
post.description:
Returns `a + b + body` as plain text with `Content-Type: text/plain`. The load generator sends bodies framed with both `Content-Length` and chunked `Transfer-Encoding`, and does not send a `Content-Type` header; both framings must be handled correctly.

**Standard:** Must use the framework standard HTTP server with default configuration. No custom TCP tuning, no experimental flags, no worker count beyond framework defaults.

**Tuned:** May adjust worker counts, thread pools, TCP socket options, and use framework-specific performance flags. Custom buffer sizes allowed.

**Infrastructure:** Configuration is free. The endpoint must be answered by a module or handler loaded into the server itself, not proxied to an application process behind it.

requestBody.description: Third integer operand as plain-text digits (e.g. `"20"`)

200.description: Sum of `a`, `b`, and the body value

get.description:
Returns the fixed plain-text string `ok` with `Content-Type: text/plain`. Used exclusively by the pipelined profile, where the load generator sends 16 requests back-to-back on each connection before awaiting responses. The trivial response body removes application-level variance so the benchmark measures pure HTTP pipeline handling throughput.

**Standard:** Must use the framework standard request handling. No custom pipeline batching or read-ahead optimizations.

**Tuned:** May implement custom pipeline batching, read buffer optimizations, or framework-specific pipelining flags.

**Infrastructure:** Configuration is free. Each request in a batch must produce its own response; coalescing the batch into one pre-built buffer, or answering from a cache keyed on the request line, is not allowed.

get.summary: Wait `ms` milliseconds, then echo the delay
get.description:
Parses `{ms}` from the path, waits that long, and responds with the parsed number as the body and `Content-Type: text/plain`. `GET /delay/0` is a valid request that must answer immediately with `0`.

The benchmark sends a flat `GET /delay/10` over 32,000 held connections, so the throughput ceiling is `connections / delay` = 3.2M rps. Validation draws its own delays after the container is up, checks that each response took at least ~90% of the requested time, that `/delay/500` takes measurably longer than `/delay/10`, and runs 32 overlapping requests with 32 different delays - the delay is per-request state, never a field on the server, connection or handler.

Prefer a real async wait (`await Task.Delay`, `tokio::time::sleep`, `asyncio.sleep`, ...). Blocking the thread is permitted but caps throughput at `threads / delay`; do not create a thread per request, and do not sleep by polling I/O.

**Standard:** Bind `/delay/{ms}` with the framework's own router and wait with the framework's own idiomatic mechanism. Blocking the request's thread for the duration is permitted, but you may not answer before the delay has elapsed, and the delay must be read from the path on every request.

**Tuned:** May use a custom timer wheel, a dedicated timer thread, coarser timer granularity, or batched expiry, so long as no response leaves before its own delay has elapsed.

**Engine:** Must derive the wait from the request path with a real timer. A fixed configured interval, a static delay directive, or anything that answers without reading `{ms}` is not an implementation of this profile.

parameters.name: ms
parameters.description: Delay in whole milliseconds. `0` means no delay.

200.description: The parsed delay, in decimal, with no surrounding whitespace or JSON. Sent no earlier than `ms` milliseconds after the request arrived.

servers.description: HTTP/1.1 + TLS - opt-in tls_check listener (probed with /json/1)

get.summary: Process dataset items and serialize JSON
get.description:
Returns the first `count` items (1-50) from the pre-loaded dataset (`/data/dataset.json`), unchanged, each with a computed `total` field (`price × quantity × m`). Responds with `Content-Type: application/json`. The `count` field in the response must equal the route parameter.

**json-tls** (port 8081, HTTP/1.1 + TLS, ALPN `http/1.1`) and **json-h2c** (port 8082, HTTP/2 cleartext) rotate across seven `(count, m)` pairs: `(1,3)`, `(5,7)`, `(10,2)`, `(15,5)`, `(25,4)`, `(40,8)`, `(50,6)`. No `Accept-Encoding` is sent.

**json-comp** (port 8080) rotates across `(25,4)`, `(40,8)`, `(50,6)` and sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip, br`. The server must compress the body with gzip or brotli and set the matching `Content-Encoding`; when no `Accept-Encoding` is sent, no `Content-Encoding` may be set. This profile is scored by a compression-weighted formula, so smaller bodies win.

The gateway profiles request `/json/{count}` without `m`, so a missing `m` must be treated as 1.

Validation draws `count` and `m` at random on every run and compares every item field by field against `data/dataset.json`, so a made-up item with a self-consistent `total` fails.

**Standard:** Must use the framework standard JSON serialization - and, for json-comp, the framework or engine's built-in response compression. json-tls must use a standard TLS stack (OpenSSL, BoringSSL, rustls, SChannel, JDK JSSE, ...). No pre-serialized or pre-compressed caches, no bypassing the framework response pipeline.

**Tuned:** May use alternative JSON libraries, tuned compression libraries, tuned TLS providers, HTTP/2 stream and window tuning, and framework-specific optimizations. The JSON body must still be serialized (and compressed) per request from live data - pre-computed response caches are not allowed on either type.

**Infrastructure:** The JSON body must be serialized per request by the handler module. A static file on disk, a literal-response config directive, or any pre-serialized response cache does not qualify. TLS must come from a standard stack and every connection must complete a real handshake.

parameters.name: m
parameters.description: Integer multiplier used to compute each item's `total` as `price × quantity × m`. Treated as 1 when absent.

parameters.name: Accept-Encoding
parameters.description: Sent by the json-comp profile only. When present, the response must be compressed.

200.description: Processed dataset items with computed totals. Compressed, with `Content-Encoding: gzip` or `br`, when the request carried `Accept-Encoding`.

Content-Encoding.description: Compression applied (json-comp). Must be absent when the client did not send `Accept-Encoding`.

post.summary: Echo the request body back verbatim
post.description:
Reads the request body and writes the same bytes back, unchanged, with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`. Used by the **8gbit** profile over HTTP/1.1 + TLS on port 8081: 10 KB bodies with `Content-Length`, a fixed offered rate of 50,000 req/s over 512 connections. The profile is scored on CPU per request and latency, gated on holding the rate.

The benchmark sends `Content-Length`, but **chunked must work too**. Validation posts random bodies of 1 B, 1 KB, 10 KB and 100 KB, chunked bodies of 10 KB and 100 KB, and an empty body (which must return `200` with an empty body), and compares every echo byte for byte. All probes use HTTP/1.1, even if port 8081 also advertises `h2`.

**Standard:** Must read the request body through the framework's standard body API and write it back through the standard response API. Streaming is allowed and encouraged. Answering without reading - a response assembled from `Content-Length`, or a canned buffer of the right size - is not an echo.

**Tuned:** May stream, use vectored writes, reuse buffers, or hand the bytes back with zero copies. The body must still be the bytes that arrived.

**Engine:** Same as above. An engine is free to splice or reuse the receive buffer directly for the response.

**Infrastructure:** A proxy may stream the body through to an origin and back, or echo it itself. Either way the bytes returned must be the bytes sent.

requestBody.description: Arbitrary bytes. 10,240 bytes in the benchmark; any size, including empty, in validation.

200.description: The request body, byte for byte

servers.description: HTTP/2 + TLS - static-h2; HTTP/3 over QUIC (UDP) - static-h3

get.description:
Serves one of 20 static assets from `/data/static/` with the `Content-Type` matching the file extension (e.g. `text/css`, `application/javascript`, `application/json`). Missing files return `404`. The load generator round-robins across all 20 URIs with `Accept-Encoding: br;q=1, gzip;q=0.8`.

Used by **static-tls** (port 8081, HTTP/1.1 + TLS, 1,024 connections), **static-h2** (port 8443, HTTP/2 + TLS, 32 streams per connection) and **static-h3** (UDP port 8443, HTTP/3, 64 streams per connection). In the gateway profiles the proxy serves `/static/*` straight from disk.

Compression is optional. When applied, it should cover the text files (CSS, JS, HTML, SVG, JSON) and skip the already-compressed binary formats (woff2, webp). Pre-compressed `.gz` (level 9) and `.br` (level 11) siblings are on disk for the 15 text files; serving them is allowed for every entry type.

**Files must follow the disk.** Validation replaces a file with different bytes of the same length while the server runs, and the next response must carry the new bytes within 2 seconds (30 seconds for infrastructure entries). It also checks every file's size, decompressed sizes, and the 404.

**Standard:** File contents may be served from memory, but the cache must be the framework's own - a documented static file handler with whatever caching it comes with. No reading the directory into a map at startup, no pre-loaded buffers, no mapping the files by hand. Compression must use the framework's standard middleware or built-in static file handler - no handmade compression code. Serving the pre-compressed `.br`/`.gz` variants on disk is allowed, by a documented framework API where one exists, and otherwise by selecting the variant off `Accept-Encoding`; the response must carry the original file's `Content-Type` and the matching `Content-Encoding`.

**Tuned:** Same cache rule as Standard: the framework's own cache, following the disk. Pre-rendered response headers are allowed, as is serving the pre-compressed variants by any mechanism, with any compression approach.

**Engine:** Same cache rule as Standard. No other restrictions.

**Infrastructure:** Configuration is free, including sendfile, `open_file_cache`, mmap and in-memory caching. Bodies must come from the mounted static directory.

TLS (and, for static-h3, QUIC) must come from a standard stack, and every connection must complete a real handshake.

parameters.name: Accept-Encoding
parameters.description: Sent by the load generator on every request

200.description: File contents with the correct `Content-Type`. May include `Content-Encoding: br` or `Content-Encoding: gzip` when compression was applied; the decompressed body must equal the file on disk.

Content-Type.description: MIME type matching the file extension: `text/css`, `application/javascript`, `text/html`, `font/woff2`, `image/svg+xml`, `image/webp`, `application/json`

Content-Encoding.description: Compression applied, if any. Only present when the response body is compressed.

get.summary: Query items from Postgres by price range
get.description:
Executes `SELECT id, name, category, price, quantity, active, tags, rating_score, rating_count FROM items WHERE price BETWEEN $1 AND $2 LIMIT $3` asynchronously, restructures `rating_score`/`rating_count` into a nested `rating` object, and serializes the result as JSON with `Content-Type: application/json`.

The benchmark sends `min=10&max=50` with `limit` rotating across 5, 10, 20, 35 and 50, over 1,024 connections. Validation draws `min`, `max` and `limit` at random, and checks that an empty range (`min=9999&max=9999`) returns `count: 0`.

Returns `{"items":[],"count":0}` when no rows match or the database is unavailable (do not return an error response). Read the connection string from `DATABASE_URL`; never hardcode it.

**Standard:** Must use an async PostgreSQL driver with standard connection pooling. Size the pool from the `DATABASE_MAX_CONN` environment variable (currently 256), not from CPU count.

**Tuned:** May use custom pool sizes, prepared statement caching, or driver-specific optimizations beyond defaults.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of items to return, clamped to 1-50. Defaults to 50.

200.description: Items matching the price range, up to `limit`. Returns an empty list when no rows match.

get.summary: Render the fortunes table as HTML
get.description:
On each request:

1. Read all 200 rows from the `fortune` table (`SELECT id, message FROM fortune`, no `ORDER BY`), using the same pool and `DATABASE_URL` as async-db.
2. Append `{ id: 0, message: "Additional fortune added at request time." }` in memory - 201 rows.
3. Sort by `message` using ordinal / byte comparison (not locale-aware).
4. Render a complete HTML document (`<!DOCTYPE html>`) with a `<table>` holding one `<tr>` per fortune, plus an optional header row.

Respond with `Content-Type: text/html` (charset optional). All messages must be HTML-escaped: row 11 contains a raw `<script>` tag, which must appear as `<script>`.

Validation checks features rather than bytes: the Content-Type, the DOCTYPE, 201-210 `<tr>` elements, the runtime-injected row, the escaping, and a body size between 18 KB and 64 KB.

**Standard:** Must render with a real template engine - documented templating syntax, interpolation, control flow, and HTML auto-escaping by default (Razor, Jinja2, ERB, Twig, html/template, Thymeleaf, Handlebars, Askama, templ, ...). The template must be a separate artifact, not inline string concatenation in the handler. No pre-rendered or cached response bodies; the template executes per request.

**Tuned:** May use any rendering strategy, including hand-rolled string building. The handler must still query the database, append the runtime row, sort, and HTML-escape per request - pre-rendered bodies and response caches are not allowed on either type.

text/html.example:
...
idmessage
11<script>alert("This should not be displayed in a browser alert box.");</script>

servers.description: HTTP/2 + TLS (baseline-h2) and HTTP/3 over QUIC (baseline-h3)

get.summary: Sum two query parameters (H2 / H3 baseline)
get.description:
Same sum computation as `/baseline11`, returned as plain text with `Content-Type: text/plain`, used by the HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 profiles. The benchmark sends `GET /baseline2?a=1&b=1`:

- **Port 8443** (HTTP/2 + TLS, ALPN `h2`) - baseline-h2, 256 and 1,024 connections × 100 streams
- **Port 8082** (HTTP/2 cleartext, prior-knowledge) - baseline-h2c, 256, 1,024 and 4,096 connections × 100 streams. The port may also answer HTTP/1.1; validation requires the response to be HTTP/2 when the client opens with the h2 preface.
- **UDP port 8443** (HTTP/3 / QUIC) - baseline-h3, 64 connections × 64 streams

Also used as the backend sum endpoint in the gateway profiles.

**Standard:** Must use the framework standard HTTP/2 + TLS (or h2c, or native QUIC/HTTP3) configuration. No custom ALPN settings or TLS cipher tuning.

**Tuned:** May optimize TLS settings, HTTP/2 stream limits, window sizes, connection parameters, and for HTTP/3 the QUIC parameters, congestion control and UDP buffer sizes.

**Infrastructure:** Configuration is free. HTTP/2 must be the server's own implementation, and QUIC must come from the server's own implementation or a standard library it is built against (quiche, ngtcp2, quictls, msquic). The endpoint must be answered by a module or handler loaded into the server itself, not proxied to an application process behind it.

Upgrades the connection to the WebSocket protocol (RFC 6455). After the `101 Switching Protocols` response, the server echoes every received message back unchanged, with the same opcode - text frames as text, binary frames as binary. The load generator sends text frames containing `"hello"` (5 bytes):

- **echo-ws** - one message in flight per connection (512, 4,096 and 16,384 connections)
- **echo-ws-pipeline** - 16 messages sent back-to-back, then 16 echoes read
- **echo-ws-limited** - 10 messages per connection, then the connection is closed and a new one upgraded (512 and 4,096 connections)

`Sec-WebSocket-Accept` must be computed per connection from the client's `Sec-WebSocket-Key`. Validation also checks binary echo, several messages in a row, a clean close handshake, and that a plain `GET /ws` without upgrade headers gets a 4xx (or a closed connection) without taking the server down.

OpenAPI 3.0 cannot model the WebSocket message exchange that follows the upgrade. Only the HTTP handshake is documented here.

**Standard:** Must use the framework standard WebSocket API with default buffer sizes. No custom batching or read-ahead optimizations. The upgrade handshake must be handled by the framework's own WebSocket support - pre-computing or caching the 101 response across connections is not allowed.

**Tuned:** May optimize WebSocket frame handling, the upgrade path, and buffer sizes, and use custom frame parsers or batched read paths, as long as every connection performs a real handshake.

101.description: Switching Protocols - WebSocket connection established. The connection switches to WebSocket framing; subsequent communication is not HTTP.

Sec-WebSocket-Accept.description: SHA-1 of the client nonce concatenated with the WebSocket GUID, base64-encoded

400.description: Request to `/ws` without valid upgrade headers (`426 Upgrade Required` or another 4xx is equally acceptable)

200.description: gRPC OK (`grpc-status: 0`, sent as a trailer). Response body is a length-prefixed, protobuf-encoded `SumReply`, e.g. `00 00000002 0803` for `result = 3`.

grpc-status.description: gRPC status code, sent as a trailer. `0` = OK.

Rating.description: Aggregated item rating. In Postgres it is stored as the `rating_score` and `rating_count` columns and must be restructured into this object.

Item.description: A single item as stored in the Postgres `items` table. Used in async-db and production-stack responses.

ProcessedItem.description: An item from the JSON dataset, unchanged, with a per-request computed `total` field. Used only in `/json/{count}` and `/public/json/{count}` responses.

total.description: Computed per request as `price × quantity × m` - integer arithmetic, no rounding

JsonResponse.description: Response from `GET /json/{count}` and `GET /public/json/{count}`. The `count` field must equal the route parameter and match `items.length`.

count.description: Number of items returned. Must equal the `count` route parameter.

DatabaseResponse.description: Response from `GET /async-db`. The `count` field must be dynamically computed from the number of returned rows, not hardcoded. Returns `{"items":[],"count":0}` when no rows match or the database is unavailable.

SumRequest.description:
Protobuf `SumRequest` message for the `GetSum` RPC. Over the wire this is a binary gRPC DATA frame - the JSON representation here is for documentation only.

```protobuf
message SumRequest { int32 a = 1; int32 b = 2; }
```

SumReply.description:
Protobuf `SumReply` response message with `result = a + b`. Over the wire this is a binary gRPC DATA frame. proto3 omits the field when `result` is 0.

```protobuf
message SumReply { int32 result = 1; }
```
